0-4834-16-t.subevent: Demonstrators in Baghdad and mainly in Sadr City took to the streets on Thursday in denunciation of lack of services, unemployment and unfair apportionment.
Public sector employees joined residents in their rally.
Oil Ministry employees called to be included in the staffing cadre just as their mates in other ministries.
Employees of the General groups firm related to the Ministry of Industry and minerals protested against the decision to cut off 20% of their salaries.
All Iraqis united over the call to improve their situation, ascertain security in the country and boost its economy.

33-2389-1-1.subevent: YouTube announced it is removing videos that push extremist views like white supremacy or deny events like the Holocaust or Sandy Hook shooting.

YouTube's new rules prohibit any video alleging that a group is superior to justify discrimination, segregation, or exclusion based on qualities like age, gender, race, caste, religion, sexual orientation, or veteran status.
YouTube refused to take down the channel of conservative personality Stephen Crowder for using homophobic slurs against journalist Carlos Maza.
YouTube said Crowder's videos didn't violate the site's rules, stating that opinions can be deeply offensive but if they don't violate policies, they'll remain on the site.
YouTube said it would remove channels that brush up against its hate speech rules from its YouTube Partner Program and reduce the reach of borderline content.
YouTube suspended monetization of Crowder's channel due to a pattern of egregious actions harming the broader community.
YouTube said Crowder could monetize his channel again if he addressed certain issues, including removing a link from the video selling his T-shirts and merchandise.
Facebook in March announced it was banning white nationalist and separatist content, but faced blowback for leaving up a doctored video of Nancy Pelosi.
The Anti-Defamation League applauded YouTube's new policy but called on the company to do more, saying the move alone is insufficient.

0-4488-1-1.subevent: Boko Haram launched its second attack on the city of Maiduguri in the early morning hours on Feb. 1.
Nigerian troops beat back the attackers and claimed to inflict hundreds of casualties.
Boko Haram took the town of Baga plus 16 surrounding villages at the beginning of the year after battling the local garrison for several hours.
After the first foiled attack on Maiduguri last week, Boko Haram captured another town, Monguno, defended by an army contingent of equal size.
Local and international experts put Boko Haram's number of active fighters at anywhere between 5,000 and 50,000.
At the height of its power in September 2014, Islamic State had an estimated 31,500 fighters, and a rough estimate puts its current strength at 25,000 troops.
Al Shabaab in Somalia still fields about 5,000 well-trained, experienced and equipped militants, according to the most recent estimates.
Boko Haram currently controls an area the size of Belgium, about half the territory of Al Shabaab.
From comparisons with similar groups, it is deduced that Boko Haram has a core strength of 7,000 to 10,000 fighters.
Boko Haram probably has an additional reserve of several thousand novice recruits and slave soldiers, with reports of ramped-up recruitment and abductions.
Nigeria, Cameroon and Chad have deployed about 35,000 troops against Boko Haram.
The article notes that insurgencies count on rough terrain and support from the local population to survive, and Boko Haram has both.
The article states that little is known about Boko Haram's financial and organizational capabilities.

1-14826-2-13.subevent: Alicia Soto attended the 1 October Sunrise Remembrance Ceremony in Las Vegas, where she has returned every year since the Route 91 Harvest music festival mass shooting.
A slideshow during the ceremony displayed the names and pictures of the 58 people killed in the shooting, including two women who died within the past year from injuries suffered in the attack.
Clark County Sheriff Joe Lombardo announced that Kimberly Gervais and Samanta Arjune would be added to the official death toll, raising the number from 58 to 60.
Lombardo said he was comfortable acknowledging that the two women lost their lives as a result of the October 1 shooting.
The ceremony had fewer attendees due to the coronavirus pandemic, with officials limiting the number of people allowed.
Governor Steve Sisolak addressed the crowd, saying that raising the limit on public gatherings this week made Thursday's event one of his biggest priorities.
Sisolak offered condolences and said, 'We will never, never forget what happened that day, or the lives that were lost, and the lives that were changed.'
Albert Rivera, father of victim Jordyn Rivera, thanked survivors for coming together and acknowledged Greg Zanis, the carpenter who built 58 crosses, who died in May.
Rivera called for unity and urged people to remember how they came together after the shooting, saying, 'It's said that it takes more effort to hate than to love. Let's remember that.'

0-4716-1-1.subevent: The social uprising in Chile has reached its fourth month, with masses of people continuing to protest and demand structural change despite ferocious repression by the militarized Carabineros police force.
Chileans are looking ahead to a plebiscite that may open the way to a new Constitution, as the dictatorship-era charter has been a major obstacle to change.

General Augusto Pinochet's 1980 Constitution institutionalized the economic and political domination of the dictatorship and enshrined a neoliberal framework that erased the role of the state in social and economic areas.

Despite 30 years of post-dictatorship elected rule and some reforms, the market model embodied in Pinochet's charter still shapes economics and politics, with privatizations perpetuating inequality and reinforcing extreme social divisions.
Chile's elected governments have not reformed or democratized the Carabineros, and the militarized police continue to treat the Chilean people as 'the internal enemy.'

Shortly after the protests began in October, President Sebastián Piñera declared 'We are at war' and called thousands of army troops to patrol the streets for the first time since the dictatorship, enforcing a 10-day curfew.
Outrage over the October crackdown spurred more massive demonstrations, with 1.2 million chilenos gathering to protest in Santiago's Plaza Italia on October 25, chanting '¡Chile despertó!'

Several international human rights delegations criticized the security forces, denouncing the deliberate intent to inflict harm on protesters rather than disperse them, with Human Rights Watch noting 'compelling evidence of excessive use of force and abuses against demonstrators and bystanders.'

The October protests put Chile's entrenched inequality in the spotlight, with studies showing significant disparities in life expectancy, income inequality, and access to health, pensions, and education.

The demonstrations since October mark a new era of social struggle defined by broad-based participation, youth involvement, and new forms and symbols of autonomous mobilization, including feminist performances, songs, murals, and memorials.
Piñera has made small concessions but has resisted any structural change to the neoliberal model, responding to social demands with repression rather than dialogue.
In January, Congress passed an 'anti-looting law' that criminalized various protest tactics, despite alarm from the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.

Two months before the scheduled plebiscite, the answer remains uncertain, with approval ratings of Chile's institutions at an all-time low and protesters expressing hopes for an end to the neoliberal system and fears that nothing will change.
The month of March will be definitive in this struggle, as Chileans return to daily life and continue to demand a new political and socioeconomic model that assures their rights.

6-19306-4-t.subevent: New official figures show that in the final quarter of 2019 the Northern Ireland economy was still 4% smaller than its 2007 peak.
The Northern Ireland economy is now facing a deep recession as a result of the ongoing coronavirus crisis.
The Ulster University Economic Policy Centre estimated that output could fall by almost 10% in 2020.
The official figures, produced by Nisra, suggested that the economy grew by 0.7% in 2019.
The Northern Ireland economy was already slowing before the crisis began.
Quarterly growth in the last three months of 2019 was just 0.2%, driven by the public sector and manufacturing.
The service sector, which is the dominant part of the economy, showed no growth.
Nisra said official statistical evidence of the scale of the economic crisis will only be clear when the figures for the second quarter of 2020 are compiled.
Those figures are not due to be released until October.

1-16475-1-1.subevent: An ancient gold coin celebrating the assassination of Julius Caesar sold for a record $3.5 million at auction.
The coin, called an 'aureus', features a portrait of Marcus Junius Brutus, one of Caesar's assassins.
The coin also depicts the daggers used by Brutus and Cassius and a cap of Liberty, with the inscription 'Eid Mar' referencing the Ides of March.
The coin was issued by Brutus in 42 BC, two years after the assassination.
Richard Beale, managing director of Roma Numismatics, described the coin as a 'naked and shameless celebration' of the assassination in a press release.
Caesar was killed by a group of senators, including friends and people he had pardoned, after being appointed dictator for life.
Brutus killed himself after losing the Battle of Philippi to Octavius and Mark Antony.
The coin is in near-mint condition and is one of only three known to exist.
The previous record for a Roman coin was set in 2008, and the previous record for any coin was set in 2012.

0-4450-1-2.subevent: A ship carrying migrants sank off the Italian island of Lampedusa.
The boat overturned shortly after midnight.
Rescuers pulled the bodies of 13 women, some of them pregnant, from the water on Monday.
The vessel capsized after many of its passengers rushed to one side as rescue boats approached.
Authorities described the ship as an overloaded and already listing boat six nautical miles from Lampedusa.
The first two bodies recovered were those of women, according to Flavio Di Giacomo of the IOM.
Di Giacomo said the boat had begun its journey in Tunisia and its passengers were predominantly Tunisians and western African migrants.

1-14826-2-14.subevent: Alicia Soto attended the 1 October Sunrise Remembrance Ceremony in Las Vegas, where she has returned annually since the Route 91 Harvest music festival mass shooting.
A slideshow at the ceremony displayed the names and pictures of the 58 people killed in the shooting, including two women who died within the past year from their injuries.
Clark County Sheriff Joe Lombardo announced that Kimberly Gervais and Samanta Arjune would be added to the official death toll, raising the number from 58 to 60.
Lombardo said he was comfortable acknowledging that the two women lost their lives as a result of the October 1 shooting.
The ceremony had fewer attendees due to the coronavirus pandemic, with officials limiting the number of people allowed.
Governor Steve Sisolak addressed the crowd, saying that raising the limit on public gatherings this week made Thursday's event one of his biggest priorities.
Sisolak offered condolences and said, 'We will never, never forget what happened that day, or the lives that were lost, and the lives that were changed.'
Albert Rivera, father of victim Jordyn Rivera, thanked survivors for coming together and acknowledged Greg Zanis, the carpenter who built 58 crosses, who died in May.
Rivera called for unity and urged people to remember how they came together after the shooting, saying, 'It's said that it takes more effort to hate than to love.'

0-4388-1-1.subevent: A new report claimed that 13 million Italians live in areas where the mafia exerts influence over everyday life.

The report, commissioned by Italy's parliamentary anti-mafia commission and produced by research institute Censis, used crime statistics to identify 610 urban and rural districts in the Italian south where clans are active.
The report stated that Italians living in those districts, even if law-abiding and not clan members, are conditioned by the mafia's capillary control.
Giuseppe Pisanu, head of the anti-mafia commission, said the Italian mafia was now 'silently prospering' by moving from spectacular crimes to business and politics.
Censis found the highest concentration of people living under the shadow of the mafia, 95.9%, in the province of Agrigento in Sicily, followed by Naples at 95%.

The four main mobs in Italy enjoy an estimated annual turnover of €130bn, but Pisanu noted that the 22% of Italians living under their shadow produced just 14.6% of Italy's GDP and held 12.4% of bank deposits.
In Catania and Palermo, 80% of shops allegedly pay protection money starting from €500 a month.
Suspicious fires in the four regions studied by Censis doubled to 8,441 a year between 1998 and 2007.
Investigators believe Italy's clans are investing more profits from extortion and drug dealing outside the Italian south, including in building work for Milan's Expo in 2015.
The Camorra and 'Ndrangheta are suspected of carving up investments in Rome, with the former focusing on suburban shopping centres and the latter on luxury property and restaurants.

Pisanu said that as authorities get better at confiscating funds in Italy, the mafias are getting better at investing overseas, and the 'Ndrangheta has even offered to act as a financial services consultant to Colombian cartels.

3-17632-4-t.subevent: Preparations are in place to receive 55 individuals, including 46 Malaysians, returning from Iran on Sunday (March 22).

Women and Family Minister Datuk Seri Rina Harun said she was satisfied with preparations at the monitoring centre here which will house the returnees, who are expected to arrive at the centre at 10.30am.
Rina said the centre will also place 23 officers involved in the mission and crew members.
Rina said there were 46 Malaysians, eight Singaporeans and one Indonesian expected.

Rina said the Social Welfare Department would work together with other agencies under her ministry to take care of those at the monitoring centre, including preparing food and providing counselling service.
The government is bringing home 46 Malaysians stranded in Iran on a special flight scheduled to touch down at KLIA2 at 6.10am Sunday.
Deputy Foreign Minister Datuk Kamarudin Jaffar said the AirAsia flight departed Tehran at 11.45 am Saturday.

2-34597-1-1.subevent: NASA's Lucy mission launched from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station at 5:34 a.m. ET on Saturday morning.
The launch team confirmed the spacecraft was safe and healthy and that Lucy successfully deployed its solar arrays.
Lucy will embark on a 12-year mission to explore Jupiter's Trojan asteroid swarms, which have never been observed.
Lucy is the first spacecraft designed to visit and observe these asteroids, which are remnants from the early days of our solar system.
Thomas Zurbuchen, associate administrator for NASA's Science Mission Directorate, commented on the importance of observing the Trojans.
The spacecraft is set to fly by an asteroid in the main asteroid belt and then explore seven of the Trojans, swinging back to Earth's orbit three times for gravity assists.
The mission is named after the Lucy fossil, and the team hopes it will help piece together the history of the solar system.
Hal Levison, principal investigator, explained that the Trojans are stable and are 'fossils of what planets formed from.'
Lucy will visit specific asteroids named after heroes from Homer's 'The Iliad': Eurybates, Queta, Polymele, Leucus, Orus, Patroclus, and Menoetius.
The Lucy spacecraft is more than 46 feet from tip to tip, with giant solar panels, and took over 500 engineers and scientists to build.
Lucy will use three science instruments to study the asteroids and will fly by them at about 15,000 miles per hour, closer than previous flybys.
After the mission, the team plans to propose an extended mission, and the spacecraft will remain in a stable orbit for over 100,000 years.

0-4448-1-1.subevent: An UAA Ukraine Air Alliance Antonov AN-12 freighter, registration UR-CAH, performing flight UKL-4050 from Vigo, Spain to Lviv, Ukraine, disappeared from radar about 7.4nm before the airport.

The aircraft was found on the ground about 0.8nm before runway 31 in soil and vegetation, near a soccer stadium and a cemetery, where the crew had attempted an emergency landing due to running out of fuel.
Five occupants were killed, and three occupants were taken to hospitals with injuries.

Ukraine's State Emergency Services reported the aircraft disappeared from radar at 07:10L, and at 07:29L one crew member called to report an emergency landing attempt; the aircraft was located at 07:40L.

The SES reported that by 09:00L it was determined there were 8 people on board, three bodies were found, three people were injured and taken to a hospital, and two people were missing; the two missing were later found perished.
Ukraine's Ministry of Infrastructure reported the aircraft was operated by 3 crew, and later added that five people were found killed and three needed to be extricated and taken to a hospital.
The Mayor of Lviv reported the crew had declared emergency due to low fuel but did not reach the runway; the aircraft was found with the cockpit cut off and cargo shifted, crushing occupants.

Ukraine's NBAAI reported the aircraft was scheduled to land in Lviv for a refueling stop, and the crew performed an emergency landing resulting in a rough landing and disaster about 1.5km before runway 31; five of eight people were killed, and an investigation was opened.
On Oct 5th 2019, the European Aviation Safety Agency revoked the airline's status as authorized third country operator, disallowing operations within EU airspace.
On Oct 7th 2019, Ukraine's Ministry of Transport announced the termination of the airline's air operator's certificate effective Oct 5th 2019.

On Oct 9th 2019, the NBAAI announced a special commission to investigate the accident; the on-site work took place Oct 5-7, black boxes were recovered and read out, and information from ground facilities was collected.
The NBAAI reported preliminary information that the aircraft was scheduled to operate from Vigo to Bursa with a refueling stop at Lviv, and that five of eight crew members were killed.
The NBAAI released their preliminary report on Dec 20th 2019, detailing the flight data recorder and cockpit voice recorder findings.
The crew did not provide critical remarks up to intercepting the localizer for runway 31, and ATIS transmitted weather and runway information.

The NBAAI described the sequence of events during final approach, including the crew reporting localizer capture, controller informing of visibility changes, and crew contacting tower and confirming landing clearance.

At 03:43:34 UTC, the aircraft's internal engines briefly increased then decreased, with vertical speed 4 m/s, height 48m (40m below glide path), and speed 244 km/h, which was 26 km/h less than the flight manual's required speed.

At about 30m height, the elevator deflected to pitch-up but was insufficient, and the aircraft collided with trees at a height of 5-7m, about 1500-1600m from the threshold, after which recording stopped.
During the flight, the navigator provided course corrections and distance reports, and the flight engineer reported altitude every 10 meters from 100m until collision.
Analysis showed the crew increased instrument speed three times by increasing vertical speed, indicating inadequate actions by the PIC.
At the accident site, investigators found the glide slope and heading alarm flags were turned off.

1-wiki-img/15491-1/15491-1-2.subevent: Mars will be at its biggest and brightest in the night sky as it lines up with Earth on the same side of the sun.
The event, known as 'opposition', occurs when Mars and the sun are on directly opposite sides of Earth.
All three bodies will be in a straight line at roughly 11.30pm.
Mars will be at its best around 1am on Wednesday, according to the Royal Observatory Greenwich.
Hannah Banyard, an astronomer at the Royal Observatory Greenwich, said it's a really good chance to view it, noting the last time this happened was 2018 but it was difficult to see.
She added that for about a month now it's been easy to see, as it rises earlier and gets quite high into the sky.
Nasa describes the phenomenon, explaining that during opposition Mars rises in the east as the sun sets in the west and sets in the west as the sun rises in the east.
Despite cloudy weather forecast for parts of the UK, Mars should be visible among breaks and even through lighter cloud, Ms Banyard added.
Ms Baynard said you should be able to see Mars with the naked eye, but recommended using a four-inch telescope with 24-millimetre magnification.
The next time Mars will be this big and bright will be 2033.

2-34752-6-1.subevent: Harmful algae usually bloom during the warm summer season or when water temperatures are warmer than usual.
Warmer water due to climate change might favor harmful algae in a number of ways.
Climate change might lead to more droughts, which make freshwater saltier, causing marine algae to invade freshwater ecosystems.
In the southwestern and south central United States, toxic marine algae have been killing fish in freshwater lakes since 2000.
Higher levels of carbon dioxide in the air and water can lead to rapid growth of algae, especially toxic blue-green algae.
Climate change might affect rainfall patterns, leading to alternating periods of drought and intense storms, causing more nutrient runoff into waterbodies.
Scientists predict that sea level could rise up to one meter by the year 2100, creating more shallow and stable coastal water.
Climate change is expected to alter the timing and intensity of coastal upwelling, potentially leading to more algal blooms along the west coast of the United States.

6-wiki-img/18504-2/18504-2-1.subevent: The Chang'e-5 orbiter module is heading back to the moon following deep space tests.
The orbiter delivered a return module containing 1.731 kilograms of lunar samples to Earth on Dec. 16 before firing its engines for an extended mission.
The Chang'e-5 orbiter entered an intended orbit around Sun-Earth Lagrange point 1 in March and carried out tests related to orbit control and observations.
Satellite trackers observed that Chang'e-5 may have altered its orbit on Aug. 30 and is destined for a lunar flyby early September 9 Eastern time.
The Beijing Aerospace Flight Control Center has not yet provided an update on the plans for Chang'e-5.
Jing Peng, deputy chief designer of the Chang'e-5 spacecraft system, said during a June conference that a visit to a planetary body such as Venus may not be possible due to a lack of propellant.
Samples collected by the Chang'e-5 lander are now being analyzed, and applications for sample materials are open to domestic and international institutions.
NASA currently has no plans to trade its Apollo-era lunar samples with those returned by China's Chang'e-5 mission, though its chief scientist expressed hope for such an exchange in the future.
China is planning a followup lunar sample-return, Chang'e-6, in 2024, with the French space agency contributing a science payload.
China's Lunar and Planetary Data System provided an update on the Chang'e-4 mission, noting that the Yutu-2 rover has covered roughly 799 metres across 33 lunar days.

23-13614-13-t.subevent: For over a year, Israel has allowed little more than basic humanitarian aid into Gaza to isolate Hamas and stop rocket fire.
A ceasefire between Israel and Hamas two months ago was meant to ease restrictions, but progress has been slow and frustration is rising.
Gaza's sewage system leaks raw sewage, and engineer Maher al-Najjar says it took months of negotiations to get Israel to allow spare parts, but modernization is blocked.
Most of Gaza's sewage cannot be treated, so tons of raw waste flow into the sea, affecting the port, fishermen, and swimmers.
Abdullah, a 27-year-old fisherman, continues to fish in polluted water because he has no other job options.
Since the ceasefire, fighting has died down but strict sanctions remain, with most of Gaza's 1.5 million people reliant on food aid and unable to enter or leave.
Tens of thousands of Gazans have lost jobs, and most industrial operations have stopped due to lack of raw materials and export restrictions.
The Pepsi plant manager Ahmed Yazji says production has been cut drastically because ingredients are hard to get, and the ceasefire brought no change.
Some improvements since the truce include more fuel and limited products like clothes and shoes entering Gaza, but the UN says they haven't significantly improved living conditions.
Israel says it intends to ease restrictions but wants assurance that Hamas will stop rocket fire; Hamas has reduced attacks but some rockets are still fired.
Israel has curtailed airstrikes, but recent inter-factional fighting among Palestinians means violence continues, though Shifa Hospital no longer receives dead and injured daily.
People worry that unless sanctions are lifted more fully, frustrations will rise and the fragile truce could collapse.

0-4716-3-1.subevent: Chile has been gripped by protests against high living costs and inequality for nearly two weeks.
Demonstrators are calling for President Sebastian Pinera to step down, and protests have continued with clashes between police and protesters.
Police have used tear gas, water cannon, rubber bullets and pellets, prompting allegations of rights abuses.
Looting has taken place and supermarkets and petrol stations have been set on fire.
At least 20 civilians have been killed, according to officials.
The protests began as a student-led demonstration against transport fares after the government announced a metro fare increase.
Economy Minister Juan Andres Fontaine said those upset with the price rise could wake up earlier and pay a lower rate, sparking outrage.
Students conducted mass fare evasion by jumping over metro turnstiles and destroying them, and protests spilled into the streets as police tried to stop them.
Metro stations, supermarkets, and petrol stations were burned, leading the president to declare a state of emergency.
Chileans are frustrated with the increasing cost of living, low wages and pensions, lack of education rights, poor public health system, and inequality.
Protesters have called for changes to the pension system, an increase in the minimum wage, Pinera's resignation, and a new constitution.
Pinera initially declared a state of emergency, which suspended certain freedoms and deployed military forces, but later lifted it and replaced eight cabinet members.
Pinera proposed new social reforms including a rise in the minimum wage, an increase in the state pension, and stabilisation of electricity costs.
Pinera backed out of hosting the APEC trade summit and COP25 climate change summit to prioritise re-establishing public order.
Officials said 20 people died as a result of the unrest, and the National Institute of Human Rights reported over 1,233 civilians injured and thousands arrested.
UN investigators arrived in the country to investigate deaths and allegations of excessive force, and Pinera welcomed them.
The head of the INDH criticised the police after a team member was shot by metal pellets, and the police director defended the police's actions.
Pinera's concessions have failed to satisfy protesters, with many vowing to stay in the streets until he steps down.

1-15327-3-t.subevent: On 12 March, a 33-year-old salesman disembarked from a flight from Dubai at an airport in southern India, feeling very sick with chills, dry cough and breathlessness.
Airport officials moved him to hospital in Trivandrum, Kerala, where they tested him for coronavirus, then sent him home to his village in Kasargod district.
When the man reached Chengala, local village council members and the local public health centre took down his details and asked him to isolate himself from his family.
Six days later, his test came back positive, but he was already in isolation; he was later taken to hospital and recovered.
Over the last month, Chengala reported 22 cases of Covid-19, quarantined more than 400 people, and 20 patients recovered and returned home.
The local village council opened a community kitchen, provided free lunches for over 1,200 people, and used a helpline and WhatsApp groups to arrange accommodation for those in isolation.
Kerala reported its first Covid-19 case in January, and the number of cases rose steadily, making it a hotspot.
More than two months after the outbreak, Kerala reported three deaths and more than 370 confirmed cases, with over 100,000 people in isolation.
Kerala imposed a lockdown a day before the nationwide one, did rigorous contact tracing, and set up Covid-19 care centres in all districts.
Health workers supported people with special needs, and counsellors made more than 340,000 telephone calls to personnel in affected areas.
Experts attributed Kerala's success to its robust public health system and grassroots democracy, with village councils enforcing mass quarantine.
Officials warned that breathless media reports of Kerala flattening the curve could be premature, as testing has been limited and delayed.
Mass screening with antibody tests has been delayed because about 100,000 kits ordered by the state haven't arrived yet.
Kerala also got lucky as the average age of infected people is 37, and most are Gulf returnees.
Kerala has one of the highest rates of communicable diseases in India, and the summer monsoon rains could trigger a spike in diseases, complicating diagnosis.
The government has worked out a detailed plan for phased opening up of the state when infections stop.
Analysts say Kerala has stuck to the script and done it well, with cases slowing down, high recoveries, and low mortality.

0-4398-1-2.subevent: Ecuador's government declared a state of emergency after protesters opposed to a fuel price hike disrupted transport nationwide.
President Lenin Moreno said he imposed the measure to ensure citizens' security and avoid chaos.
Protesters were angered by Mr Moreno's decision to end 40-year-old subsidies for fuel, which he said were no longer affordable.
On Thursday students and the transport sector led a national strike.
Taxi, bus and truck drivers blocked roads and bridges in Quito and Guayaquil, bringing transport to a standstill.
Some protesters clashed with police, who fired tear gas to disperse crowds, and Interior Minister Maria Paula Romo said 19 people had been arrested.
Some protesters burned tyres and threw objects at armoured police vans, drawing criticism from Mr Moreno.
The president said he would not allow protesters to impose chaos.
Under the emergency measure, Mr Moreno's government can restrict freedoms and deploy the armed forces to maintain order.
The elimination of the fuel subsidies, introduced in the 1970s, are part of Mr Moreno's plan to shore up Ecuador's flagging economy and ease its debt burden.
Ecuador's government agreed to cut public spending as part of a loan deal with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), signed in March, allowing Ecuador to borrow $4.2bn.
On Tuesday, Ecuador announced it was leaving OPEC to pump more oil and raise revenue.

24-31161-1-t.subevent: Transgender weightlifter Laurel Hubbard competed at the Tokyo Olympics but failed to complete any of her first three lifts, ruling her out of medal contention in the women's over-87-kilogram division.
China's Li Wenwen won the women's over-87-kilogram weightlifting division with a total of 320 kilograms.
Hubbard made a heart gesture to the audience before leaving the competition arena.
Hubbard thanked the IOC, the International Weightlifting Federation, and the people of Japan for hosting the Games during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Hubbard overbalanced on her opening lift of 120 kilograms, had her second attempt of 125 kilograms ruled invalid, and failed her third attempt.
Emily Campbell won silver in the women's over-87-kilogram division, becoming the first British woman to win a weightlifting medal.
Sarah Robles of the United States won bronze with 282 kilograms, becoming the first U.S. woman with two weightlifting medals.
The IOC in 2015 drew up recommendations for including transgender athletes, and the IWF implemented similar policies, including a testosterone requirement that Hubbard met.
The IOC announced it will release a new framework for transgender athletes' eligibility in the coming months.
The New Zealand Olympic Committee acknowledged the sensitivity of gender identity in sport and reaffirmed its commitment to supporting eligible athletes.
Earlier Monday, Wang Zhouyu won the women's 87-kilogram category for China, with Tamara Salazar and Crismery Santana taking silver and bronze.

0-4347-1-1.subevent: Bed Bath & Beyond Inc. increased its projected store closures for the fiscal year to 60, up from the April estimate of 40.
Company officials said most of the closings are expected after the holiday shopping season in early 2020 during a quarterly earnings call on Wednesday.
Interim CEO Mary Winston said 40 of the stores closing will be Bed Bath & Beyond stores and 20 will be stores in the company's other concepts.
Winston said the 'fleet optimization' will increase profitability and create a better balance between physical and digital presence.
As of the end of August, the company had 1,534 stores, including 993 Bed Bath & Beyond stores, 277 World Market stores, 126 buybuy Baby stores, 81 Christmas Tree Shops stores, and 55 Harmon stores.
Winston said there are plans to renegotiate all leases and that $350 million of inventory at retail will be removed from stores before the 2019 holiday season through markdowns and clearance events.
Coresight Research reported that nearly 8,600 store closures have been announced across the retail sector so far this year, up from around 5,900 in 2018.
Coresight estimates closures could reach 12,000 by the end of the year.

0-4569-4-1jpg.subevent: A former Fort Worth, Texas, police officer has been indicted by a grand jury for murder in the death of Atatiana Jefferson.
Jefferson, 28, was shot and killed in October when Officer Aaron Dean fired through a window.
Dean, 35, was arrested in October, but all police shootings go before a grand jury, which issues charges.
Dean was in the backyard of Jefferson's home when he shot Jefferson through a window after responding to a call from a neighbor about the front door of the house being open.
Dean, who joined the Fort Worth Police Department in April 2018, resigned two days after the shooting and just hours before being arrested and charged with murder.
According to Dean's original arrest affidavit, Jefferson was inside a bedroom playing video games with her 8-year-old nephew moments before the shooting.
The 8-year-old boy told police his aunt heard noises outside and that she grabbed her handgun.

Bodycam video from Dean's perspective showed the former officer walking around the home, shining a flashlight into a window and shouting 'Put your hands up! Show me your hands!' and less than a second later firing a shot.
Investigators confirmed that Dean did not identify himself as an officer at any point.

Less than three weeks after Jefferson's murder, and nearly two months before the grand jury decision, the judge presiding over Dean's case — David Hagerman — issued a gag order surrounding the proceedings.
Hagerman's order prevents anyone connected with the case from making statements about witnesses, evidence or any opinion about Dean's guilt or innocence.

2-34826-6-t.subevent: Turkey recognized Kazakhstan as the first country to do so.
Turkey and Kazakhstan institutionalized their relations through many agreements and protocols after Kazakhstan's independence.
Kazakhstan became one of Turkey's most significant political and economic partners in the region.
Turkey and Kazakhstan signed a Strategic Partnership Agreement during President Nursultan Nazarbayev's visit to Turkey in October 2009.
The High Level Strategic Cooperation Council (HLSCC) was established during then Prime Minister Recep Tayyip Erdoğan's visit to Kazakhstan in May 2012.

The first meeting of the HLSCC was held on 11-12 October 2012 during President Nazarbayev's visit to Turkey, and the second meeting was held during President Erdoğan's visit to Kazakhstan on 15-17 April 2015.
The bilateral trade volume between Turkey and Kazakhstan reached almost 3.9 billion dollars in 2019, with a common target of 10 billion dollars.

Turkish entrepreneurs in Kazakhstan have been active in food, medication-chemistry, construction, hotel management, and manufacturing sectors, with Turkish construction companies completing projects worth 23.5 billion dollars by 2019.
Turkey and Kazakhstan cooperated to institutionalize the Summit of Turkic Speaking States, and Kazakhstan played a significant role in establishing the Turkic Council and TURKPA.
Kazakhstan hosts the International Turkic Academy established within the Turkic Council.
About 8,000 students study at the International Hodja Ahmet Yesevi Turkish-Kazakh University campuses in four cities.

12-wiki-img/8552-1/8552-1-1.subevent: Afghanistan said it would keep its main crossings with Iran open despite the coronavirus threat.
Faisal Javid, a spokesman for President Ashraf Ghani's national security adviser, said the border is open to allow medical checks and quarantine of affected returnees.
Javid added that sealing official routes would push people to use illegal crossings, allowing contaminated individuals to enter undetected.
Officials reported that 141 people have tested positive for the virus in Afghanistan, with at least four deaths in the past month.
A ministry official said the virus was brought to Afghanistan by economic migrants fleeing Iran due to joblessness and the state of the economy.

Waheed Mayar, a Public Health Ministry spokesman, said closing the border would lead to more positive cases, danger, and deaths via illegal routes.
Authorities increased preventive measures along the border, including checking all returnees and isolating those affected.
Authorities extended the lockdown in Herat by three more weeks and enforced a curfew in Kabul.
Residents expressed concerns about the spread of the virus, with shopkeeper Fateh Shah saying they can only pray and take measures not to get affected.

2-34513-5-t.subevent: Lebanese Prime Minister Najib Mikati announced on Twitter that Friday would be a day of public mourning.
Six Shi'ites were shot dead in Beirut in an attack on supporters of Hezbollah and an allied Lebanese party.
The supporters were gathering to demand the removal of the judge investigating last year's devastating Beirut port blast.

6-18755-14-1.subevent: The Madras High Court's Madurai Bench lifted the ban on TikTok, subject to conditions.
The bench vacated its interim order banning the app, with conditions that pornographic videos will not be uploaded, failing which contempt of court proceedings would begin.
TikTok issued a statement expressing gladness about the decision and welcoming it for its community in India.
Earlier this month, the high court issued an interim order banning the downloading of the app in India and restricting media from telecasting videos taken using it.
Tamil Nadu's IT Minister M. Manikandan had earlier said the state would write to the central government seeking a ban on the app.
The high court appointed leading lawyer Arvind Datar as an independent counsel to the court.
On an appeal by the Chinese company, the Supreme Court on April 22 asked the Madras High Court to decide on TikTok's plea for interim relief by April 24, failing which the ban would stand lifted.
TikTok said it was committed to continuously enhancing its safety features and expressed gratitude for the opportunity to continue serving users better.

1-16189-3-1.subevent: Venezuelan consumer prices rose 800 percent in 2016 while the economy contracted by 18.6 percent, according to preliminary central bank figures seen by Reuters.

The extended slump in oil prices turned Venezuela's oil-boom economy into a mirror of the latter day Soviet Union, with rampant product shortages leading people to skip meals and wait hours in food lines.
President Nicolas Maduro's government blamed the situation on an 'economic war' led by political adversaries with the help of the United States.
The central bank stopped releasing quarterly and monthly economic indicators as problems mounted.
The oil sector shrank 12.7 percent in 2016, and the non-oil sector shrank by 19.5 percent, according to an excerpt of a document containing the figures.
A source with firsthand knowledge said the figures could be changed in the process of approval by the central bank's board of directors.
In 2015, the economy contracted 5.7 percent while inflation reached 180.9 percent, the central bank said last year.
Maduro accused opposition-linked businesses of artificially creating economic problems and said inflation is the result of speculative price-gouging by unscrupulous capitalists.
Maduro said during a news conference that minimum wage increases in 2016 totaled 454 percent and were well above 2016 inflation, without offering an inflation figure.
Venezuelans last year began crossing into neighboring Brazil and Colombia to buy groceries due to currency controls that left businesses unable to obtain dollars.

Investor concern that Venezuela may not be able to service its foreign debt made its bonds among the highest-yielding emerging market securities, paying investors on average 21 percentage points more than similar U.S. Treasury notes.
Maduro dismissed rumors that the country or state oil company PDVSA could default, noting that the ruling Socialist Party has never missed a bond payment.

32-2285-2-1.subevent: A driver in Oakland told the author about a billboard featuring Kawhi Leonard with the message 'The King of the North is Coming' before Game 3.

Steph Curry and Draymond Green expressed disappointment after Game 4, with Green saying 'This sucks.'
Nick Nurse said the Raptors 'flipped a switch about Game 2 against Orlando' rather than in the Finals.
The Raptors lost Game 1 to the Magic but then won the next four games by an average of nearly 19 points.

After losing the first two games to the Bucks, the Raptors won four straight, including a double-overtime Game 3.

After Game 4, Kyle Lowry stopped to take a selfie with a young Warriors fan who had stayed behind.

9-21834-8-1.subevent: Millions of Americans, including President Trump, attended religious services online on Sunday due to social distancing measures.

Megachurches streamed their Sunday services online through apps, websites, and YouTube.
Trump tweeted about watching a service by Pastor Jentezen Franklin, who preached to an empty auditorium and thanked Trump.
Greg Laurie's church saw over 230,000 online attendees, with over 1,400 people committing to follow Jesus.
LifeBridge Community Church offered online services with curbside prayer.
Dr. Alveda King urged Americans to 'Don't panic. Pray.' and planned to attend service in person with precautions.
Smaller churches faced decisions about holding services, with some like St. Philip AME Church holding services with precautions.
Religious leaders took unprecedented actions, including bishops dispensing with Mass attendance requirements and the Mormon Church halting all worship services worldwide.
The Vatican announced all public Masses in Italy are forbidden, and Pope Francis visited St. Mary Major Basilica to pray for the sick.

17-28164-3-1.subevent: Dale Coyne Racing announced a collaboration with Rick Ware Racing for a full-time entry and a part-time entry in the 2021 NTT IndyCar Series.
Coyne revealed that his second full-time entry, now #51, will be run in partnership with Rick Ware.

The primary sponsor of the #51 car will be announced in February, with the driver expected to be announced next week.
Ex-Formula 1 driver Romain Grosjean is favorite for the seat, although his participation in IndyCar's four oval races remains open to question.
Ware said he met Dale last year through their Indy efforts and thought a long time about expanding into IndyCar.

11-22309-3-t.subevent: Clergy groups in Muskogee are working to establish a fund to support a local mother who recently lost five of her children in a shooting in the city.

1-14808-1-t.subevent: Businessman and TV host Zef Eisenberg died while attempting to break a British land speed record at Elvington Airfield in Yorkshire, northern England.

1-wiki-img/15302-2/15302-2-1.subevent: Armenia's forces hit Ganja, Azerbaijan's second-largest city, killing and injuring dozens of Azerbaijani civilians, less than a day after a humanitarian ceasefire between Yerevan and Baku came into effect.

6-19298-5-10.subevent: Kumbh Mela is the largest peaceful congregation of pilgrims on earth, during which participants bathe or take a dip in a sacred river.
Devotees believe that by bathing in the Ganges one is freed from sins liberating her/him from the cycle of birth and death.
Millions of people reach the place without any invitation.
The congregation includes ascetics, saints, sadhus, aspirants-kalpavasis and visitors.
The festival is held at Allahabad, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nasik every four years by rotation and is attended by millions of people irrespective of caste, creed or gender.
Its primary bearers, however, belong to akhadas and ashrams, religious organizations, or are individuals living on alms.
Kumbh Mela plays a central spiritual role in the country, exerting a mesmeric influence on ordinary Indians.
The event encapsulates the science of astronomy, astrology, spirituality, ritualistic traditions, and social and cultural customs and practices, making it extremely rich in knowledge.
As it is held in four different cities in India, it involves different social and cultural activities, making this a culturally diverse festival.
Knowledge and skills related to the tradition are transmitted through ancient religious manuscripts, oral traditions, historical travelogues and texts produced by eminent historians.
However, the teacher-student relationship of the sadhus in the ashrams and akhadas remains the most important method of imparting and safeguarding knowledge and skills relating to Kumbh Mela.

5-5883-1-1.subevent: The European Space Agency is starting what it expects to become a regular series of small science missions.
The first winning 'S-Class' idea will receive 50 million euros and will be readied for launch in 2017.
Esa hopes particularly to encourage young scientists and research teams from smaller member states.
Prof Mark McCaughrean said the S-Class missions would help train people and give smaller member states the opportunity to lead missions.
Interested parties must submit expressions of interest by 23 March, followed by a defined proposal in June.
A clutch of the best ideas will probably be selected for study in November, with a winner chosen for implementation 12 months after that.
The S-Class mission must fit within Esa's 'Cosmic Vision' strategy document.
The national governments of winning scientists will almost certainly be backing the projects as well, perhaps funding the cost of instrument development.
More realistic mission concepts could include compact space telescopes or fundamental physics experiments in Earth orbit.
A good example is the 8m-euro Lares spacecraft launched in February on Esa's new Vega rocket.
Another example is Esa's own Proba-2 satellite, which incorporates an imager from Belgium called Swap that is taking scientifically very useful pictures of the Sun.
Swap was in action last week, tracking the solar storm that hurled billions of tonnes of plasma at Earth.
In complete contrast, Esa is about to select its next large, or 'L-Class', mission.
Three ideas are competing: a big X-ray telescope, a probe to Jupiter and its moons, and another general relativity experiment to detect gravitational waves.

26-13936-2-1.subevent: Millions of students, workers and scientists came together at the global climate strikes last week.

General Assembly session in New York.

0-4325-2-1.subevent: The opioid crisis continues to worsen as new types of drugs, including fentanyl, find their way onto the streets.

A photograph taken at the New Hampshire State Police Forensic Laboratory shows a lethal dose of heroin (about 30 milligrams) on the left and a 3-milligram dose of fentanyl on the right, enough to kill an average-sized adult male.
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention states that fentanyl is up to 100 times more potent than morphine and many times more potent than heroin.
Drug users generally don't know when their heroin is laced with fentanyl, so they can inadvertently take a deadly dose.
Dealers include fentanyl to improve potency, but their measuring equipment usually isn't fine-tuned enough to avoid overdose levels.
Street fentanyl is almost always made in clandestine labs, making it less pure and more unpredictable in its effects.

Tim Pifer, director of the New Hampshire State Police Forensic Laboratory, told STAT that heroin and fentanyl look identical, and users don't know what they're taking, comparing injection to 'a loaded gun.'
New Hampshire saw 439 drug overdoses in 2015, most related to opioids, with about 70 percent of opioid-related deaths involving fentanyl.
The state has seen 200 deadly opioid overdoses this year so far, according to Pifer.
Fentanyl was originally used as an anesthetic, then doctors started using it for pain relief in small quantities.
With trained professionals and laboratory-grade equipment, fentanyl has a wide therapeutic index.
The difference in strength between heroin and fentanyl arises from differences in their chemical structures.
Both chemicals bind to the mu opioid receptor in the brain, but fentanyl gets there faster than morphine because it more easily passes through brain fat.
Fentanyl hugs the receptor so tightly that a tiny amount is enough to start the molecular chain of events that instigates opioids' effects on the body.

3-17502-3-t.subevent: The Portuguese Episcopal Conference announced on Jan. 21 that public Masses would be suspended in Portugal from Jan. 23 due to the 'extreme gravity' of the coronavirus crisis.

1-15874-5-1.subevent: A new mission proposal suggests a relocatable lander could explore Saturn's moon Titan.

1-16165-3-2.subevent: The Australian Grand Prix has been called off because of coronavirus.

9-20780-1-1.subevent: Google suspended the Parler social networking app from its Play Store until the platform adds robust content moderation.

0-4403-2-2.subevent: Mickaël Harpon stabbed colleagues at the Paris police headquarters and was shot dead on Thursday.

The number of childcare hours for which the benefit is received depends on the hours worked by the parent with the fewest working hours, with a maximum of 230 hours per month per child.
If the applicant or their benefit partner participates in a training programme, reintegration programme, or civic integration course, they may also be entitled to the childcare benefit.

If the family lives in an EU country, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, or Switzerland, and the children attend a childcare centre in that country, the applicant may also be entitled to the benefit, provided the conditions are met.
A foreign childcare centre must be registered, and the applicant can check the register of foreign childcare to see if their centre is registered.
The applicant can apply for the childcare benefit themselves, and information on how to do this is available.
The applicant must notify the authorities of any changes in details used to calculate the benefit, such as income or childcare hours, and information on how to do this is available.

22-wiki-img/3685-3/3685-3-4.subevent: France has been at the forefront of a burgeoning pan-European far-right movement.
Marine Le Pen, an anti-immigration Eurosceptic, may top the first round of France's presidential election on 23 April.
The under-30s in France are more nationalistic than the general population.

Génération Identitaire (GI), a group of identitarians, specializes in publicity stunts filmed and posted online to advertise its fight to reclaim French territory said to have been lost to foreign migrants.
GI has 120,000 Facebook fans, almost twice as many as the youth wings of the Socialist Party and the centre-right Republicans combined.
GI leader Pierre Larti, 26, engages in verbal confrontation with North African men while handing out flyers in Paris.
GI is sprouting branches across Europe, seeing the continent as a battleground between European and Islamic culture.
Jean-Yves Le Gallou, a former Euro-MP, speaks of a struggle for 'civilisational' identity and has produced a video entitled Being European that has been viewed more than 3.2m times on YouTube.
Le Gallou's website Polemia stands at the high-brow end of France's identitarian spectrum, and his continued influence is testament to the deep intellectual roots of the movement.
Identitarians have thrived on the web over the past decade, with Fdesouche, a news aggregator, getting about 3m views per month.
Fdesouche's success has spawned a swarm of imitators and rivals, collectively called the 'fachosphère'.
Alain Soral's website Égalité et Reconciliation (E&R) weaves nationalist and left-wing themes, and has more readers than Fdesouche.
Soral rejects accusations of anti-Semitism, distinguishing between 'ordinary Jews' and the 'organized Jewish lobby'.
At Sciences Po, Eurosceptic students have set up a club, 'Critique of European Reason' (CRE), to wage the fight against liberal elites.
CRE leader Nicolas Pouvreau says the group has managed to create a Eurosceptic safe space in a hostile environment.
Last year's Brexit vote thrilled CRE members, who gathered outside the UK embassy to drink champagne and sing God Save the Queen.
CRE members regard uncontrolled migration and trade flows as a source of social disintegration.
Kevin, a CRE student supporting hard-left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon, says he has often been called 'dirty white' and says the mainstream press denies the reality of 'anti-white racism'.
Ugo Iannuzzi, a Sorbonne student, says he has suffered from being white and has often cried, feeling bad about being French and loving his origins.
Alexandre Devecchio, a journalist, calls those preoccupied with the erosion of identity the 'Zemmour generation', named after Eric Zemmour who argues that the 1968 revolt has led France to ruin.
Devecchio says many twentysomethings agree with Zemmour because they feel let down, experiencing unemployment, insecure jobs, and a sense of physical and cultural insecurity.
Marine Le Pen lacks the backing of a major party and is expected to be defeated by any second-round opponent.
Polls suggest that half the voters backing hard-left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon would either abstain or back Le Pen in a second round against Emmanuel Macron.
Identitarianism feeds on pessimism, and the country's patriotic rebels are young and may have time on their side.
